units.text: INT. WOMAN - CONTINUOUS
Very few.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Miss Worsley would not let you kiss her.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Are you sure?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Quite.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: What do you think she’d do if I kissed her?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Either marry you, or strike you across the face with her glove. What would you do if she struck you across the face with her glove?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Fall in love with her, probably.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Then it is lucky you are not going to kiss her!
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Is that a challenge?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: It is an arrow shot into the air.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Don’t you know that I always succeed in whatever I try?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I am sorry to hear it. We women adore failures. They lean on us.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: You worship successes. You cling to them.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: We are the laurels to hide their baldness.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: And they need you always, except at the moment of triumph.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: They are uninteresting then.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: How tantalising you are!
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: A pause .
Lord Illingworth, there is one thing I shall always like you for.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Only one thing? And I have so many bad qualities.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Ah, don’t be too conceited about them. You may lose them as you grow old.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: I never intend to grow old. The soul is born old but grows young. That is the comedy of life.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: And the body is born young and grows old. That is life’s tragedy.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Its comedy also, sometimes. But what is the mysterious reason why you will always like me?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: It is that you have never made love to me.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: I have never done anything else.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Really? I have not noticed it.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: How fortunate! It might have been a tragedy for both of us.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: We should each have survived.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: One can survive everything nowadays, except death, and live down anything except a good reputation.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Have you tried a good reputation?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: It is one of the many annoyances to which I have never been subjected.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: It may come.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Why do you threaten me?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: I will tell you when you have kissed the Puritan.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Enter Footman .
Tea is served in the Yellow Drawing-room, my lord.
units.name: FRANCIS

units.text: Tell her ladyship we are coming in.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Yes, my lord.
units.name: FRANCIS

units.text: Exit .
Shall we go in to tea?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Do you like such simple pleasures?
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: I adore simple pleasures. They are the last refuge of the complex. But, if you wish, let us stay here. Yes, let us stay here. The Book of Life begins with a man and a woman in a garden.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: It ends with Revelations.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: You fence divinely. But the button has come off your foil.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH
